parameters.covariate_model: see Roy and Varin 2004 (transcription pending verification)

extraction.tier_rationale: Succinylcholine plasma PK is dominated by rapid BCHE-mediated hydrolysis; published compartmental parameters vary by assay and are not openly reconciled. Curated as the substrate anchor for the BCHE pharmacogenomic modifier; KERNEL PENDING.

parameters.label: plasma hydrolysis clearance (BCHE-mediated)
parameters.covariate_model: BCHE-dependent; atypical phenotype reduces hydrolysis (see pharmacogenomic_modifiers)

pharmacogenomic_modifiers.caveat: The prolonged block is well-documented; the SCALE (x0.2 on hydrolysis clearance) is ILLUSTRATIVE and highly individual — it encodes the phenotype's direction and rough magnitude, NOT a precise clearance. Homozygous atypical patients can have apnea lasting hours; the honest message is 'expect prolonged block / prepare', never a computed dose.

extraction.tier_rationale: Kinetic modifier (Tier-D by construction): reduced BCHE hydrolysis -> prolonged succinylcholine effect for a given dose. Substrate-scoped to BCHE substrates only (excludes remifentanil/amide-LA/rocuronium). Opt-in, forward-only.

pharmacogenomic_safety_flags.consequence: markedly prolonged neuromuscular block (succinylcholine apnea, hours in the homozygous atypical patient)
pharmacogenomic_safety_flags.action: EXPECT and prepare for prolonged block; consider an alternative relaxant. This is an awareness flag, NOT a dose adjustment.

extraction.tier_rationale: The avoidance/awareness dimension of atypical BCHE: prolonged block is the clinically load-bearing fact (prepare, do not titrate). Carried as a flag (no number) alongside the kinetic modifier, because BCHE is genuinely both.

pharmacogenomic_safety_flags.consequence: malignant hyperthermia — a life-threatening hypermetabolic crisis
pharmacogenomic_safety_flags.action: AVOID succinylcholine (and volatile agents) in an MH-susceptible patient.

extraction.tier_rationale: Succinylcholine is an MH trigger (CPIC). A susceptibility, never a kinetic change — a hard avoidance flag with no dose effect.
